html:
Stephen the Great was prince of Moldavia from 1457 to 1504, who fought off the Ottomans, Hungarians, Poles and Tatars and is remembered as the greatest Romanian ruler of the Middle Ages.

He took the throne with help from his cousin Vlad the Impaler. In January 1475 he crushed a large Ottoman army at Vaslui, one of the worst Ottoman defeats of the time, and the Pope praised him as an athlete of Christ. He later lost the Black Sea ports of Kilia and Cetatea Albă and agreed to pay tribute. He built dozens of churches and monasteries, including Putna, where he is buried, and his successors began the painted churches. The Romanian Orthodox Church made him a saint in 1992. He ruled from Suceava in Moldavia.
sum: Stephen the Great was prince of Moldavia from 1457 to 1504, who fought off the Ottomans, Hungarians, Poles and Tatars and is remembered as the greatest Romanian ruler of the Middle Ages.
